50340.text: If a paramagnetic bar is brought near a bar magnet, then it is

Repelled by both the poles of the bar magnet
Attracted by the South-pole and repelled by the North-pole of the bar magnet
Attracted by the North-pole and repelled by the South-pole of the bar magnet
50340.sol: Paramagnetic materials have a tendency to move from a region of weak magnetic field to a region of strong magnetic field. When a paramagnetic bar is brought near either pole of a bar magnet, it gets weakly magnetized in the direction of the external magnetic field. This induced magnetization causes the near end of the bar to develop an opposite magnetic polarity to that of the adjacent pole of the bar magnet. Therefore, the paramagnetic bar is attracted by both the North and South poles of the bar magnet. Answer: A

59552.text: A container consists mixture of four gases as 5 ~g~ H ₂, 8 ~g~ He , 50 ~g~ CO ₂ and 20 g Ne at a certain temperature. Which of the following gases exerts minimum partial pressure? ( array |c|c|c|c|c| X =x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 P ( X =x) & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0.4 array )
59552.sol: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures states that the partial pressure of each gas in a mixture is the product of its mole fraction and the total pressure: P_i = X_i P_ total . Since P_ total is constant, the partial pressure is proportional to the mole fraction, which depends on the number of moles: X_i = n_i n_ total . Therefore, the gas with the fewest moles exerts the minimum partial pressure. Moles are determined from mass and molar mass using n = mass molar mass . The molar masses are: 2 g/mol for H ₂ , 4 g/mol f

reflects red light and absorbs blue and green light.
73958.sol: Chlorophyll, the pigment responsible for the green color of leaves, primarily absorbs blue and red light wavelengths from the visible spectrum. The green light, which is not absorbed effectively by chlorophyll, is reflected and gives leaves their characteristic green colour.

79365.subject: Botany
79365.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body. Statement II: Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II arre true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
79365.sol: Primary xylem is of two types – protoxylem and metaxylem. Arrangement of protoxylem and metaxylem: In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type of primary xylem is called endarch. In roots , the protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch .

80493.subject: Botany
80493.text: What is the fate of the male gametes discharged in the synergid?
options: One fuses with the egg, other(s) degenerate(s) in the synergid.
One fuses with the egg, other(s) fuse(s) with synergid nucleus.
One fuses with the egg and other fuses with central cell nuclei.
80493.sol: After a pollen grain germinates on the surface of the stigma, it forms a pollen tube that grows through the style and is guided through the micropyle (a minute opening at one end of the ovule). The pollen tube grows toward and into one of the synergid cells, which begins to degenerate as the pollen tube enters it (or shortly before). The pollen tube then ceases growth, ruptures, and releases its two sperm cells, which migrate to the egg and central cell, fertilization of which gives rise to the embryo and endosperm

84392.text: Given below are statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
84392.sol: On the basis of location, the nephrons, are of two types, in majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla. Such nephrons are called cortical nephrons and form 85% of the total nephrons. In some of the nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla. These nephrons are called juxta medullary nephrons and form 15% of the total nephrons.

84648.subject: Zoology
84648.text: What happens during fertilization in humans after many sperms reach close to the ovum?
options: Secretions of acrosome helps one sperm enter cytoplasm of ovum through zona pellucida
All sperms except the one nearest to the ovum lose their tails
Cells of corona radiata trap all the sperms except one
Only two sperms nearest the ovum penetrate zona pellucida
84648.sol: The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilization. During fertilization, a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum and induces changes in the membrane that blocks the entry of additional sperms. Thus, it ensures that only one sperm can fertilize an ovum. The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane.

Injections or Implants: It is a type of hormonal method in which the hormones like progestogens (similar to progesterone) are injected into the women’s bloodstream subcutaneously while in implants it is placed under the skin. 105281.subject: Physics
105281.text: When a p-n junction diode is subjected to a reverse bias, which of the following correctly describes the effect on the depletion region and the dominant mechanism of current?
options: The depletion width increases and drift current dominates.
The depletion width increases and diffusion current dominates.
The depletion width decreases and drift current dominates.
The depletion width decreases and diffusion current dominates.
105281.sol: In a reverse-biased p-n junction, the applied voltage acts in the same direction as the built-in barrier potential. This pulls majority carriers away from the junction, increasing the width of the depletion region and the barrier height. The increased barrier effectively stops the diffusion of majority carriers across the junction. Consequently, the small reverse current that flows is entirely due to the drift of minority charge carriers swept across the junction by the strong electric field in the depletion region

105551.sol: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_ = h - Since K_ = eV₀ , we can write: eV₀ = h - V₀ = ( h e ) - e Comparing this with the equation of a straight line y = mx + c , the slope m of the V₀ versus graph is: S = h e h = eS The intercept on the frequency axis (x-axis) is the threshold frequency ₀ , which occurs when V₀ = 0 : 0 = ( h e ) ₀ - e = h ₀ Substituting h = eS , we get: = eS ₀ Thus, Planck's constant is eS and the work function is eS ₀ . Answer: eS and eS ₀

121977.sol: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid. Gemma cups are found in Bryophytes. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals. The sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule.

122846.subject: Botany
122846.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The roots can be modified for support, storage of food and respiration. Reason: Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122846.sol: Roots are modified for support, storage of food and respiration. Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food.

123040.subject: Botany
123040.text: In some plants, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle. These are known as adventitious roots. Which of the following plants exhibits this type of root system?
123040.sol: Roots that arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle are called adventitious roots. According to NCERT, examples of plants with adventitious roots include grass, Monstera, and the banyan tree. Mustard and gram are dicotyledonous plants that exhibit a tap root system, which develops from the direct elongation of the radicle. Wheat is a monocotyledonous plant that exhibits a fibrous root system, where roots originate from the base of the stem. Answer: Monstera

123131.subject: Botany
123131.text: Which of the following is the correct floral formula for the floral diagram given below?
123131.sol: The given floral diagram is of Family Fabaceae. Flower - zygomorphic, bisexual. Sepals - five, fused. Petals - five, polypetalous, papillionaceous corolla. Androecium - ten, diadelphous. Gynoecium - ovary superior, monocarpellary, unilocular, marginal placentation, with many ovules.

123575.subject: Botany
123575.text: Which type of cells in plants are known to undergo mitotic cell division?
123575.sol: Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cells. However, there are few exceptions to this where haploid cells divide by mitosis, for example, male honey bees. Against this, the plants can show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells. From your recollection of examples of alternation of generations in plants (Chapter 3) identify pla

123599.subject: Botany
123599.text: What are the small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres called?
123599.sol: By this stage, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope. This then, is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied.At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that

123684.subject: Botany
123684.text: What is the name of the structures formed during diplotene, which are recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers?
123684.sol: Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene, leaving the chromosomes linked at the sites of crossing over. The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures, are called chiasmata. n oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.

124007.subject: Botany
124007.text: How do polar molecules move across the membrane?
124007.sol: One of the most important functions of the plasma membrane is the transport of the molecules across it. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it. Many molecules can move briefly across the membrane without any requirement of energy and this is called the passive transport. Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by the process of simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, i.e., from higher concentration to the lower. Water may also move across this membrane f

124264.subject: Botany
124264.text: What does ‘S’ refer to in a 70S and an 80S ribosome?
124264.sol: Svedberg’s Unit or sedimentation coefficient refers to S in a 70S and an 80S ribosome.

124270.subject: Botany
124270.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Mesosomes in bacteria are considered homologous to the mitochondria of eukaryotes. Reason (R): Mesosomes contain respiratory enzymes and help in cellular respiration. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
124270.sol: Assertion (A) is incorrect because mesosomes and mitochondria are analogous structures, not homologous. Analogous structures perform the same function but have different structural origins (mesosomes are extensions of the prokaryotic plasma membrane, whereas mitochondria are double-membrane bound eukaryotic organelles). Reason (R) is correct because mesosomes contain respiratory enzymes and perform the function of cellular respiration in bacteria, which is functionally similar to what mitochondria do in eukaryotes.

124490.subject: Botany
124490.text: How is growth typically measured in a maize root apical meristem?
124490.sol: Growth, at a cellular level, is principally a consequence of increase in the amount of protoplasm. Growth is, therefore, measured by a variety of parameters some of which are: increase in fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number.

125459.subject: Botany
125459.text: Which molecule does RuBisCO have a greater affinity for when the CO2: O2 ratio is nearly equal?
125459.sol: Let us try and understand one more process that creates an important difference between C3 and C4 plants – Photorespiration. To understand photorespiration we have to know a little bit more about the first step of the Calvin pathway – the first CO2 fixation step. This is the reaction where RuBP combines with CO2 to form 2 molecules of 3PGA, that is catalysed by RuBisCO. RuBisCO that is the most abundant enzyme in the world is characterised by the fact that its active site can bind to both CO2 and O2 – hence the nam

125915.subject: Botany
125915.text: In what condition do unisexual flowers prevent self-pollination?
options: When both types of flowers are on the same plant
When both male and female flowers are on different plants
When the stigma and anther are positioned differently
125915.sol: Outbreeding Devices: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower In some other species, the anther and stigma are placed at different positions so that the pollen cannot come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. This is a genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the

126252.subject: Botany
126252.text: What are the respective ploidy levels of an antipodal cell, a secondary nucleus, and a primary endosperm nucleus in a typical angiosperm?
126252.sol: Antipodal cells are part of the female gametophyte (embryo sac) and are haploid ( n ). The secondary nucleus is formed by the fusion of two polar nuclei in the central cell prior to fertilization, making it diploid ( 2n ). The primary endosperm nucleus is formed by the fusion of a haploid male gamete with the diploid secondary nucleus (triple fusion), making it triploid ( 3n ). Therefore, the correct sequence of ploidy levels is Haploid, Diploid, and Triploid. Answer: Haploid, Diploid, Triploid

127075.subject: Botany
127075.text: In almost all Indian metropolitan cities like Delhi, the major atmospheric pollutant(s) is/are:
127075.sol: In almost all Indian metropolitan cities like Delhi, the major atmospheric pollutants are SO ₂, NO ₂ and particulate matter in which the SPM (Suspended Particulate Matter) in Delhi's air exceeds the permitted levels by over 100 % .

127098.subject: Botany
127098.sol: The regulator gene is responsible for the synthesis of a protein called repressor. The repressor may be active or inactive (aporepressor). The active repressor is normally seen in inducible systems while aporepressor is seen in repressible system. The repressor has an affinity for operator gene.

127173.subject: Botany
127173.text: What is the relationship between species richness and area for different taxa, according to Alexander von Humboldt's observations?
options: Species richness decreases with increasing area
Species richness remains constant with increasing area
Species richness increases with increasing area, but only up to a limit
Species richness decreases logarithmically with increasing area

In fact, the relation between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa (angiosperm plants, birds, bats, freshwater fishes) turns out to be a rectangular hyperbola (Figure13.2). On a logarithmic scale, the relationship is a straight li

127270.subject: Botany
127270.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice, and 1,000 varieties of mango. Reason: A single species might show high diversity at the genetic level over its distributional range.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127270.sol: A single species might show high diversity at the genetic level over its distributional range. India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice, and 1,000 varieties of mango.

127437.subject: Botany
127437.text: Which of the following are fused in somatic hybridization involving two varieties of plants?
127437.sol: Protoplast of two varieties of plants are fused in somatic hybridization.

128327.subject: Zoology
128327.text: What hormone plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body along with TCT?
128327.sol: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/demineralisation). PTH also stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and increases Ca2+ absorption from the digested food. It is, thus, clear that PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone, i.e., it increases the bloodCa2+ levels. Along with TCT, it plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body. The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind

128408.sol: A, B respectively are Portal circulation and Anterior pituitary

128511.subject: Zoology
128511.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta 2. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system 3. Thymosins only provide cell mediated immunity 4. Thymosins only provide humoral immunity
128511.sol: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system

128575.subject: Zoology
128575.text: Choose the correct option among the following options Column I Column II A. Epinephrine i. Increase in muscle growth B. Testosterone ii. Decrease in blood pressure C. Glucagon iii. Decrease in liver glycogen content D. Atrial natriuretic factor iv. Increase in heart beat

128725.subject: Zoology
128725.sol: Peyer's patches are present in ileum. They are organised lymphoid follicles. They form an important part of the immune system by monitoring intestinal bacteria populations. They prevent the growth of pathogenic bacteria in the intestine.

128904.subject: Zoology
128904.text: What is the significance of the sounds produced during each cardiac cycle?
options: They are of no clinical diagnostic significance
They are of limited clinical diagnostic significance
They are of great clinical diagnostic significance
128904.sol: During each cardiac cycle two prominent sounds are produced which can be easily heard through a stethoscope. The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves whereas the second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves. These sounds are of clinical diagnostic significance.

128921.subject: Zoology
128921.text: Which layer is comparatively thin in veins?
128921.sol: The blood flows strictly by a fixed route through Blood Vessels—the arteries and veins. Basically, each artery and vein consists of three layers: an inner lining of squamous endothelium, the tunica intima, a middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibres, the tunica media, and an external layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibres, the tunica externa. The tunica media is comparatively thin in the veins .

129639.subject: Zoology
129639.text: Hormone Effect on Kidney A. Aldosterone 1. Increases reabsorption of sodium B. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) 2. Increases calcium reabsorption C. ANP (Atrial Natriuretic Peptide) 3. Reduces sodium reabsorption D. Parathyroid Hormone 4. Increases water reabsorption
129639.sol: Aldosterone increases the reabsorption of sodium in the kidneys. ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) promotes water reabsorption to concentrate urine. ANP (Atrial Natriuretic Peptide) reduces sodium reabsorption to lower blood pressure. Parathyroid Hormone increases calcium reabsorption in the kidneys.

options: Alveolar capillaries, basement substance, and alveolar epithelium
Alveolar epithelium, basement substance, and alveolar capillaries
Endothelium of alveolar capillaries, basement substance, and squamous epithelium
Squamous epithelium, basement substance, and endothelium of alveolar capillaries
129858.sol: gradient is present for CO2 in the opposite direction, i.e., from tissues to blood and blood to alveoli. As the solubility of CO2 is 20-25 times higher than that of O2, the amount of CO2 that can diffuse through the diffusion membrane per unit difference in partial pressure is much higher compared to that of O2. The diffusion membrane is made up of three major layers namely, the thin squamous epithelium of alveoli, the endothelium of alveolar capillaries and the basement substance (composed of a thin basement membr

130092.subject: Zoology
130092.text: Read the following statements regarding respiratory volumes and capacities: Statement A : Total Lung Capacity (TLC) minus Residual Volume (RV) equals Vital Capacity (VC). Statement B : Inspiratory Capacity (IC) includes the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV). Statement C : The volume of air involved in breathing movements can be estimated by using a spirometer. Statement D : Residual Volume (RV) can be directly measured
130092.sol: Statement A is correct: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. TLC = Vital Capacity (VC) + Residual Volume (RV). Therefore, TLC - RV = VC. Statement B is incorrect: Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. It includes Tidal Volume (TV) and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV). It does not include ERV. Statement C is correct: The volume of air involved in breathing movements can be esti

130473.subject: Zoology
130473.text: Match List I with List II regarding the number of bones in different regions of the adult human vertebral column. List I List II A. Cervical vertebrae I. 12 B. Thoracic vertebrae II. 5 C. Lumbar vertebrae III. 1 (fused) D. Sacrum IV. 7 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
130473.sol: The vertebral column of an adult human is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae. The number of bones in different regions are: Cervical vertebrae: 7 Thoracic vertebrae: 12 Lumbar vertebrae: 5 Sacrum: 1 (formed by the fusion of 5 sacral vertebrae) Therefore, the correct match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III. Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

130571.subject: Zoology
130571.text: What is a popular brand of condoms for males in India?
130571.sol: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted

131293.subject: Zoology
131293.text: During the human menstrual cycle, a surge in luteinising hormone (LH) induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle, resulting in ovulation. Following this event, the remaining parts of the ruptured follicle transform into a specific structure. Identify this newly formed structure and the primary hormone it secretes to maintain the endometrium.
options: Graafian follicle and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
131293.sol: After ovulation, the remaining parts of the ruptured Graafian follicle transform into a temporary endocrine structure called the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium in preparation for a possible implantation and pregnancy. Corpus albicans is a degenerated, non-functional form of the corpus luteum. LH is secreted by the anterior pituitary to trigger ovulation, not by the corpus luteum. The Graafian follicle is the mature p

131493.subject: Zoology
131493.text: What is the direction of polymerization catalyzed by DNA-dependent DNA polymerases?
131493.sol: For long DNA molecules, since the two strands of DNA cannot be separated in its entire length (due to very high energy requirement), the replication occurs within a small opening of the DNA helix, referred to as replication fork. The DNA-dependent DNA polymerases catalyze polymerisation only in one direction, that is 5' 🡪 3' . This creates some additional complications at the replication fork. Consequently, on one strand (the template with polarity 3'🡪5'), the replication is continuous, while on the other (the temp

options: Remove/Replace 2′ OH group with some other group in deoxy ribose
131767.sol: Removing 3′ OH group in deoxyribose will lead to the prevention of polymerization with 5’ end.

131772.subject: Zoology
131772.text: Which was the last human chromosome to be completely sequenced:
131772.sol: The sequence of chromosome 1 was completed only in May 2006, this was the last of the 24 human chromosomes to be sequenced.

131840.sol: The i gene is a regulatory gene that is expressed constitutively to synthesize the repressor protein. Therefore, (A) matches with (III). The operator region is the specific DNA sequence where the active repressor protein binds to prevent transcription. Therefore, (B) matches with (IV). The promoter is the sequence where RNA polymerase binds to initiate transcription of the structural genes. Therefore, (C) matches with (II). The inducer (lactose or allolactose) binds to the repressor protein, inactivating it so that

132495.subject: Zoology
132495.text: A couple, both of whom are carriers for the sickle-cell trait, wish to know the risk of their future child being affected by the disease. What is the percentage probability that their child will be affected, and what is the exact molecular defect the affected child will possess?
options: 25%, substitution of Glutamic acid by Valine in the beta-globin chain
50%, substitution of Glutamic acid by Valine in the beta-globin chain
25%, substitution of Valine by Glutamic acid in the beta-globin chain
25%, reduced synthesis of the beta-globin chain
132495.sol: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive genetic disorder. If both parents are carriers (heterozygous, Hb^A Hb^S ), the genetic cross is Hb^A Hb^S Hb^A Hb^S . The possible offspring genotypes are Hb^A Hb^A (25% normal), Hb^A Hb^S (50% carriers), and Hb^S Hb^S (25% affected). Thus, the probability of having an affected child is 25%. The molecular defect in an affected individual ( Hb^S Hb^S ) is the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain of the haemogl

132708.subject: Zoology
132708.text: How does a change in the medium composition affect a colony of bacteria?
options: It causes the entire colony to die
It causes all bacteria to adapt simultaneously
It allows only the part of the population that can survive under new conditions to thrive
It has no effect on the colony
132708.sol: The essence of Darwinian theory about evolution is natural selection. The rate of appearance of new forms is linked to the life cycle or the life span. Microbes that divide fast have the ability to multiply and become millions of individuals within hours. A colony of bacteria (say A) growing on a given medium has built-in variation in terms of ability to utilise a feed component. A change in the medium composition would bring out only that part of the population (say B) that can survive under the new conditions. In

132772.subject: Zoology
132772.text: Select the correct statement about the type of evolution shown by these structures.
options: They are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions.
Analogous structures are a result of divergent evolution.
Examples of analogy are vertebrate hearts and brains.
132772.sol: They are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions. Hence, analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution - different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity.

134020.text: What are the requirements in tissue culture?
134020.sol: Plant tissue culture medium should generally contain macronutrients, micronutrients, vitamins, amino acids or nitrogen supplements, carbon source, (sucrose and other carbohydrates) growth regulators and solidifying agents (agar-agar).

134119.text: Can bacterium be used to make human insulin?
134119.sol: Management of adult-onset diabetes is possible by taking insulin at regular time intervals. What would a diabetic patient do if enough human- insulin was not available? Now, imagine if bacterium were available that could make human insuli

134723.subject: Zoology
134723.text: In a cloning experiment, a foreign DNA is inserted into the coding sequence of the -galactosidase gene of a plasmid vector. The transformed bacteria are then plated on a suitable agar medium containing a chromogenic substrate. Which of the following correctly describes the colour of the colonies formed by the recombinant and non-recombinant bacteria?

Recombinants: Blue colonies; Non-recombinants: White colonies
Both recombinants and non-recombinants form blue colonies
Both recombinants and non-recombinants form white colonies
134723.sol: Insertion of a foreign DNA into the coding sequence of the -galactosidase gene leads to insertional inactivation of the enzyme. As a result, the recombinant bacteria cannot produce functional -galactosidase and fail to cleave the chromogenic substrate, thereby forming colourless (white) colonies. 134874.subject: Zoology
134874.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The stickiness of DNA ends produced by certain restriction enzymes facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA ligase. Reason (R): Restriction endonucleases cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate an

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
134874.sol: Assertion (A) is true because the sticky ends form temporary hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts. This brings the DNA fragments close together, which facilitates the joining action of DNA ligase to form phosphodiester bonds. Reason (R) is also true because restriction enzymes that produce sticky ends do so by cutting the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. However, Reason (R) explains how sticky ends are forme

6a104ff78b46719ce7976ccd.subject: Physics
6a104ff78b46719ce7976ccd.text: A constant force F = (4 i + 2 j ) N acts on a particle. The position vector of the particle as a function of time t is given by r = (t³ i - 2t² j ) m . The instantaneous power delivered by the force at t = 2 s is:
6a104ff78b46719ce7976ccd.sol: The position vector of the particle is given by r = (t³ i - 2t² j ) m . The velocity of the particle is the rate of change of its position vector: v = d r dt = d dt (t³ i - 2t² j ) = (3t² i - 4t j ) m/s At t = 2 s , the velocity is: v = 3(2)² i - 4(2) j = (12 i - 8 j ) m/s The force acting on the particle is F = (4 i + 2 j ) N . The instantaneous power delivered by the force is given by the dot product of force and velocity: P = F v = (4 i + 2 j ) (12 i - 8 j ) P = (4)(12) + (2)(-8) = 48 - 16 = 32 W Answer: 32 W

6a104ffb8b46719ce7976d2d.subject: Biology
6a104ffb8b46719ce7976d2d.text: A chemical compound 'X' closely resembles a normal substrate 'S' in its molecular structure. When 'X' is introduced into a biological system, it competes with 'S' for the substrate-binding site of the enzyme, leading to a decline in overall enzyme action. 6a104ffb8b46719ce7976d2d.sol: The phenomenon described is competitive inhibition, where a chemical compound (inhibitor) closely resembles the normal substrate in its molecular structure and competes for the active site of the enzyme. A well-known practical application of competitive inhibition is the control of bacterial pathogens. For example, sulfa drugs (such as sulfanilamide) act as competitive inhibitors of the enzyme that uses para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) to synthesize folic acid in bacteria. By inhibiting this enzyme, the drugs prevent

6a104ffd8b46719ce7976d64.text: During transcription, the sequence of the template strand of a transcription unit is given as: 5' - C G A T A G C C G T A T G C A - 3' Which of the following represents the correct sequence of the newly synthesized RNA transcript?

Writing the given template strand in the 3' 5' direction, we get: 3' - A C G T A T G C C G A T A G C - 5' The newly synthesized RNA transcript will be complementary and antiparallel to the template strand. 86144.subject: Chemistry
86144.text: 1,2-dimethylbenzene on treatment with chromic oxide in acetic anhydride at 273 - 283 K followed by hydrolysis produces P. P on heating with concentrated NaOH followed by hydrolysis provides Q. The functional groups present in the product Q are:
options: One carboxylic acid and one alcohol
One aldehyde and one carboxylic acid
86144.sol: 1,2-dimethylbenzene reacts with CrO₃ in acetic anhydride at 273 - 283 K to form a gem-diacetate intermediate at both methyl groups. 309417.subject: Chemistry
309417.text: When ethane-1,2-dioic acid is heated with concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ , the products formed are:
options: CO + CO ₂ + H ₂ O
309417.sol: Ethane-1,2-dioic acid is commonly known as oxalic acid, with the chemical formula HOOC-COOH . Concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ acts as a strong dehydrating agent. When oxalic acid is heated with concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ , it undergoes dehydration to yield carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and water. The chemical reaction is given by: HOOC-COOH conc. H ₂ SO ₄, CO + CO ₂ + H ₂ O Thus, the products formed are CO , CO ₂ , and H ₂ O . Answer: CO + CO ₂ + H ₂ O

304728.subject: Physics
304728.text: Suppose a planet is travelling in an elliptical orbit around the sun. The work done on the planet by the sun's gravitational force
options: is zero for one full revolution
is zero along any small segment of the orbit
is zero in no portion of the motion
is zero during certain parts of the orbit
304728.sol: The gravitational force exerted by the sun on a planet is a central and conservative force. For any conservative force, the work done over a closed path is zero. Since one full revolution corresponds to a closed path, the total work done on the planet during one complete revolution is zero. Thus, option (1) is correct. 305748.text: For an oxygen sample at 300 K , determine the average time required for a molecule to cover a distance equal to the diameter of the earth.
305748.sol: The average speed of a gas molecule is given by: v_ avg = 8RT M For an oxygen ( O₂ ) molecule at 300 K : R = 8.314 J K ⁻¹ mol ⁻¹ T = 300 K M = 32 10⁻³ kg mol ⁻¹ Substituting the values: v_ avg = 8 8.314 300 32 10⁻³ 445.5 m s ⁻¹ The diameter of the earth is D = 2 6400 km = 12800 km = 12.8 10^6 m . The average time required to cover this distance is: t = D v_ avg = 12.8 10^6 445.5 28731 s Converting the time into hours: t = 28731 3600 hours 7.98 hours 8 hours

Numbering in the opposite direction (away from the double bond) would give it locant 5. Therefore, we number towards the double bond: C1 has the -OH group, and C2=C3 is the double bond. Gluconic acid (X) can be further oxidized to saccharic acid (Y) by oxidizing its primary alcohol group at the other end of the chain. 6a7a1ff8f36cc75b211080ca.text: Consider the following four relations defined on the set of integers Z : R₁ = (x, y) Z Z : x^2 + y^2 is an even integer R₂ = (x, y) Z Z : xy 0 R₃ = (x, y) Z Z : |x - y| 3 R₄ = (x, y) Z Z : x divides y Which of the above relations is an equivalence relation?
6a7a1ff8f36cc75b211080ca.sol: An equivalence relation must be reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. For R₁ : Reflexivity: For any x Z , x^2 + x^2 = 2x^2 , which is always an even integer. Thus, x R₁ x . Symmetry: If x^2 + y^2 is even, then y^2 + x^2 is also even. Thus, x R₁ y y R₁ x . Transitivity: x^2 + y^2 is even if and only if x and y have the same parity (both are even or both are odd). If x R₁ y and y R₁ z , then x has the same parity as y , and y has the same parity as z . This implies x and z have the same parity, so x^2 + z^2 is even.
